title: Reliability and calibration of epistemic verdicts
question: How often are the sampled epistemic verdicts (guaranteed / possible / knows-that / inevitable defeat) wrong, and how do they depend on the number of worlds, the world size and |Π|?

seeds.choice: X16 seed block 13000 (plan §1.5); the long-run truth is computed by running the X13 search code from each decision point of these games, not by reusing X13's seeds

metric_definitions.decision point: (game, round t), t = 1..5; knowledge at the moment the round-t allocation was chosen (observation_at stage 'decision')
metric_definitions.verdicts: over the sampled worlds W_t and Π_t: possible = ∃π∃w win; guaranteed = ∃π∀w win; knows_win_exists = ∀w∃π win; inevitable_defeat = ∀π∀w ¬win; win ⇔ expected share > 0.5
metric_definitions.truth row: Π_t evaluated in the TRUE world at the decision point (engine replay, the timeline's evaluation stream) — the timeline's truth_victory_possible
metric_definitions.long-run truth L_t: 1 iff the best of {X13-style search plan from the true decision-point state, every plan of the full Π_t, the player's own continuation} has mean expected share > 0.5 over 20 fresh cascade/media streams
metric_definitions.targets: possible, knows_win_exists: ∃π∈Π_t wins (row) / L_t; guaranteed: the witness plan wins in the true world (row, de re) / L_t; inevitable_defeat: no π∈Π_t wins (row) / ¬L_t. For guaranteed, missed-truth (row) uses '∃π∈Π_t wins'
metric_definitions.false_assert: P(target false | verdict asserted) — soundness failure
metric_definitions.missed_truth: P(verdict not asserted | target true) — completeness failure
metric_definitions.p_hat: best_plan.win_fraction: fraction of the sampled worlds in which the best plan (most wins, ties by mean share) wins
metric_definitions.graded outcomes: victory = the game's official victory; best_wins = the best plan wins in the true world (truth row); long_run = L_t
metric_definitions.brier: mean (p̂ − y)²; murphy = reliability − resolution + uncertainty on the W+1 distinct p̂ values
metric_definitions.overconfidence: OC = mean (p̂ − y)·sign(p̂ − ½) over p̂ ≠ ½; > 0 = over-confident
metric_definitions.calibration: logistic recalibration y ~ a + b·logit(p̂), p̂ clipped to [1/(2W), 1−1/(2W)]; b < 1 = over-confident (pooled cells only: 400 cluster-bootstrap resamples for its CI)
metric_definitions.ci95: 2.5/97.5 percentiles of a cluster bootstrap over games (2000 resamples); wilson95_unclustered treats decision points as independent (too narrow)

tests.family: X16 pre-registered contrasts at n = 1600, Π = all: guaranteed W64 vs W8 (assert rate: exact McNemar paired by decision point; false-assert: cluster-bootstrap p), over-confidence at W16 (cluster-bootstrap p of OC ≠ 0); Holm over all items

tests.name: guaranteed false-assert (truth row, de re) W64 − W8 (pooled)
guaranteed false-assert (truth row, de re) W64 − W8 (bayes)
guaranteed false-assert (truth row, de re) W64 − W8 (top3)
over-confidence OC at W16 vs y = victory (pooled)
over-confidence OC at W16 vs y = best_wins (pooled)
over-confidence OC at W16 vs y = long_run (pooled)

library_identity.rule: discrete fields exact, floats |Δ| ≤ 1e-5 (GPU float32 is not bit-reproducible)

library_timeline_cpu_vs_gpu.note: library timeline_with_diagnostics, 5 decision points, 1,600-voter worlds, full Π; BayesPlanner games (CPU run: game, electorate and worlds on CPU; GPU run: all on the GPU)

deviations: Device cuda:0 (hard-pinned, lead's instruction; cuda:1 and cuda:2 are used by others), per-process cap 12 GB.
Full grid as planned (4 worlds × 3 world sizes × 3 plan-set sizes, BayesPlanner and Top-3, 50 seeds each); no reduction was needed.

World generation runs on the CPU (§1.1 point 5 exception): the library draws every synthetic world with CPU generators and only then moves it to the GPU, and this draw is ≈ 85 % of a timeline's cost. It runs in a spawn process pool (8 × 1 thread); everything else (history replay, poll filter, plan evaluation, truth row, long-run search) runs on the GPU. The pooled sampler re-implements consistent_worlds with pre-generated chunks and is checked against the library (checks.library_identity).

§1.1 point 4 (batch the worlds of all decision points) is not done: WorldBatch.step applies one plan list to all worlds of a batch, and Π_t differs per round, so joining rounds would need a library change (not approved). The worlds × plans × voters of each decision point are batched; GPU utilisation is low because the GPU work per timeline is small (≈ 0.1–0.4 s) next to the CPU world generation.

The |Π| = 8 and 16 verdicts are read from the first k columns of the full-Π outcome matrix (policy_set(…, max_policies=k) is a prefix and outcome columns are independent of the other plans under common random numbers; unit test + checks.library_identity against timeline_with_diagnostics(…, max_policies=k)).

Identity checks compare discrete fields exactly and floats within 1e-5: GPU float32 sums are not bit-reproducible (the library differs from itself by ~1 ulp in some cells, checks.library_identity.library_vs_library_bit_identical).

Long-run truth: X13's own rows cannot be reused (different seeds, they start at round 1 with the ORACLE manifesto), so the X13 search code (same CEM / hill-climb settings) is run from every decision point of the X16 games with the player's committed manifesto and state, warm-started with the full Π_t and the player's own continuation; the final re-evaluation uses 20 fresh WorldBatch streams of the true electorate (not x_batch.run_batch).
Graded outcome: the plan says 'the realised outcome'; the primary y is the game's official victory, and two further targets are reported (the best plan wins in the true world; L_t).

CPU↔GPU parity uses BayesPlanner games and the library timeline at 16 and 64 worlds of 1,600 voters (3 seeds); count metrics (rounds with a verdict, 0–5) use abs tolerance 0.25 or 5 % (x_parity.parity_rel).

Per-cell 'sample_seconds' in timing.per_cell are main-process waits on the CPU pool (overlapped with the long-run search), not CPU cost; the CPU vs GPU time per library timeline is timing.library_timeline_cpu_vs_gpu.
